title: Accounting Standard 18 Related Party Disclosures
outcomes: Explain why related party relationships need disclosure.
Identify related parties using control and significant influence.
Recognise parties that are not related and the exemptions.

meta.exam_tip: For each party, write the link (control, significant influence, KMP, relative) before deciding; aggregate family holdings.

concepts.title: Why related party disclosures matter
body: Related party relationships can affect an enterprise's results and position: prices may not be at arm's length, and transactions may occur that would not happen between unrelated parties.

AS 18 requires disclosure of these relationships and transactions so that users can understand their effect. It applies to reporting enterprises other than those exempted (smaller enterprises get relief in certain disclosures).
concepts.analogy: Readers need to know when the other side of a deal is not really a stranger.
concepts.work: A subsidiary buying raw material from its parent at above-market prices shifts profit between them.

concepts.title: Control, significant influence and who is a related party
body: Parties are related if, at any time in the period, one can control the other or exercise significant influence over its financial and operating decisions.

Control: owning (directly or through subsidiaries) more than half the voting power; or controlling the composition of the board; or a substantial voting interest with power by statute or agreement to direct financial and operating policies.

Significant influence: participating in financial and operating policy decisions without control — through board representation, policy participation, material inter-company transactions, interchange of managers or dependence on technical information. Holding 20% or more of voting power, directly or indirectly, is presumed to give significant influence.

AS 18 covers: holding companies, subsidiaries and fellow subsidiaries; associates and joint ventures; individuals with control or significant influence and their relatives; key management personnel (KMP) and their relatives; and enterprises over which any of these individuals has significant influence.
Relative: the spouse, parents, children and siblings (brother, sister) of the individual, where they could sway, or be swayed by, the individual in dealings with the enterprise.
concepts.analogy: Look for anyone who can steer or substantially sway the enterprise's decisions — and their close family.
concepts.work: A director's sister's firm that sells to the company is a related party.

concepts.title: Parties that are not related merely because of dealings
body: The following are not related parties merely because of their dealings: two companies that merely share a director (a link arises only if that director can shape the policies of both); a single customer, supplier, franchisor, distributor or agent with whom a significant volume of business is done; and providers of finance, trade unions, public utilities and government departments in normal dealings.
concepts.analogy: Economic dependence is not the same as a relationship.
concepts.work: A bank that lends to the company and insists on covenants is not a related party.

concepts.title: Exemptions from disclosure
body: No disclosure is required in consolidated financial statements for intra-group transactions, which are eliminated.
State-controlled enterprises need not disclose relationships and transactions with other state-controlled enterprises.
Disclosure is not required where it would conflict with a duty of confidentiality under a statute, regulator or similar authority — such as a bank's duty about customer accounts.
concepts.analogy: Some relationships are already visible or legally confidential.
concepts.work: A public sector bank does not list its dealings with other public sector undertakings.

concepts.title: What must be disclosed
body: Where control exists, disclose the name of the related party and the nature of the relationship, whether or not there were transactions.

If there were transactions, disclose: name of the party; description of the relationship; description of the transactions; volume, as an amount or proportion; other elements needed to understand them; year-end balances (as amounts or proportions) with any doubtful debt provision against them; and amounts written off or written back.
Items of a similar nature may be aggregated by type of related party, except where separate disclosure is needed to understand the effect.

Typical transactions: purchases or sales of goods and fixed assets, rendering or receiving services, agency arrangements, leasing, transfer of research, licences, finance (loans and equity), guarantees and management contracts.
concepts.analogy: Name, relationship, transaction, amount, balance — the five things to tell.
concepts.work: A loan to a director's firm must be disclosed with the year-end balance even if interest-free.

illustrations.title: Mapping the related parties
illustrations.q: Alpha Ltd. holds 80% of Beta Ltd.; Beta holds 30% of Gamma Ltd. Mr. Sethi holds 12% of Alpha and his wife 10%. Mr. Rao is Alpha's managing director; his brother owns Delta Traders, which supplies Alpha. Alpha also sells 35% of its output to Omega Ltd., an unrelated buyer. Identify Alpha's related parties.

head: Party
Reason
Related?
rows: Beta, controlled by Alpha, holds 30% — significant influence (Alpha's effective interest ₹24%)
With his wife he holds ₹22% — significant influence
Owned by a relative of KMP; can be influenced
Only a major customer — economic dependence is not a relationship
solution.title: AS 18 relationships

checks.label: Voting power of Mr. Sethi with his wife (%)
Effective interest of Alpha in Gamma through Beta (%)

illustrations.title: Drafting the disclosure
illustrations.q: During the year Alpha Ltd. (total sales ₹800 lakh) sold goods worth ₹40 lakh to Beta Ltd., of which ₹6 lakh is outstanding; paid Mr. Rao remuneration of ₹30 lakh; and bought goods worth ₹15 lakh from Delta Traders. Outline the disclosure.

head: Related party
Relationship
Transaction
Volume
Outstanding
rows: Enterprise of a relative of KMP
solution.title: Related party transactions

solution.text: Also disclose names and nature of relationships where control exists (Beta Ltd.), even if there were no transactions. In Alpha's consolidated statements, the sale to Beta is eliminated and need not be disclosed.

checks.label: Sales to Beta as % of Alpha's sales

jobs.title: Building the related party list
jobs.situation: A client gives a list of five related parties, but board minutes mention several other entities.
steps: Identify KMP and their relatives' businesses.
Match the ledger for transactions with each party.
Check balances and write-offs for disclosure.
jobs.takeaway: The completeness of the related party list is the auditor's first test.

mcqs.q: Holding 20% or more of voting power of an enterprise is presumed to give:
mcqs.explain: Under AS 18 an investing party holding, directly or indirectly, 20% or more of voting power is presumed to have significant influence unless it is clearly shown otherwise. More than half usually gives control. In practice: count indirect holdings too.
mcqs.topic: Control, significant influence and who is a related party

mcqs.q: Which relative is included in the AS 18 definition?
mcqs.explain: AS 18 defines relative as the spouse, parents, children and siblings of the individual, where they could sway or be swayed by the individual in dealings with the enterprise. Wider family members are excluded. In practice: list only these relations.
mcqs.topic: Control, significant influence and who is a related party

mcqs.q: Two companies with a common director are:
options: Not related merely for that reason
Related only if the director is MD of both
mcqs.explain: A common director alone does not create a related party relationship; the facts must show control or significant influence. AS 18 lists this as an example of parties not necessarily related. In practice: examine actual influence.
mcqs.topic: Parties that are not related merely because of dealings

mcqs.q: A company sells 60% of its output to one distributor. The distributor is:
options: Not a related party merely because of economic dependence
mcqs.explain: A single customer or distributor with whom a significant volume of business is done is not a related party simply because of that dependence. Some other link of control or influence is needed. In practice: disclose dependence elsewhere if material.
mcqs.topic: Parties that are not related merely because of dealings

mcqs.q: In consolidated financial statements, intra-group sales:
options: Need not be disclosed as related party transactions
mcqs.explain: AS 18 exempts intra-group transactions from disclosure in consolidated statements because they are eliminated on consolidation. They are still disclosed in the separate statements of each group company. In practice: check which set you are preparing.

mcqs.q: Where control exists, the name of the related party and nature of relationship are disclosed:
options: Whether or not there were transactions
mcqs.explain: AS 18 requires disclosure of the name and nature of the relationship wherever control exists, irrespective of transactions, because control itself can affect the enterprise. In practice: always name the parent and subsidiaries.

mcqs.q: Mr. Kumar holds 9% of a company and his father 13%. Together they hold:
options: Control, as family holdings are doubled
mcqs.explain: The holdings of an individual and his relatives are considered together: 9% + 13% = 22%, which is over the 20% presumption for significant influence, though not control. In practice: aggregate family holdings.
mcqs.topic: Control, significant influence and who is a related party

mcqs.q: Which is NOT a related party of a company?
options: A trade union representing its workers
mcqs.explain: Trade unions, providers of finance, public utilities and government departments in the ordinary course are not related parties merely because of their dealings. KMP, fellow subsidiaries and associates are. In practice: apply the list.
mcqs.topic: Parties that are not related merely because of dealings

mcqs.q: Which element must be disclosed for related party transactions?
options: Amounts outstanding at the balance sheet date
The tax paid by the related party
mcqs.explain: AS 18 requires disclosure of amounts or proportions outstanding at the balance sheet date and related doubtful debt provisions, together with name, relationship, transaction description and volume. In practice: reconcile balances with the party.

mcqs.q: A public sector undertaking need not disclose its transactions with:
options: Its own subsidiaries in separate statements
mcqs.explain: AS 18 exempts state-controlled enterprises from disclosing relationships and transactions with other state-controlled enterprises. Other related parties still require disclosure. In practice: the exemption is narrow.

summary: Related: control or significant influence at any time in the period.
Control > 50% votes, board control, or substantial interest with power; significant influence presumed at 20%.
Covers group, associates, JVs, individuals, KMP, relatives and their enterprises.
Not related merely by dealings: common director, big customer, financiers, unions, utilities.
Exemptions: intra-group in CFS; state-controlled with each other; statutory confidentiality.
Disclose name, relationship, transaction, volume, balances, write-offs; control always.
traps: Economic dependence is not a relationship.

quickref.v: Spouse, son, daughter, brother, sister, father, mother

viva.q: When are two parties related under AS 18?
viva.model: When at any time during the period one party can control the other or exercise significant influence over its financial and operating decisions.
Participation in the financial and operating policy decisions of an enterprise without control; 20% or more of voting power is presumed to give it.

viva.q: Name some parties that are not related merely by dealings.
viva.model: Two companies with a common director, a major single customer or supplier, providers of finance, trade unions, public utilities and government departments.

viva.q: What must be disclosed where control exists?
viva.model: The name of the related party and the nature of the relationship, irrespective of whether there were any transactions.

viva.q: Who is a relative under AS 18?
viva.model: The individual's spouse, parents (father, mother), children (son, daughter) and siblings, where they could sway or be swayed by the individual in dealings with the enterprise.

cases.title: Shree Ganesh Mills Ltd.
cases.case: Shree Ganesh Mills Ltd. buys cotton worth ₹2 crore from a firm owned by the CFO's wife, gives an interest-free loan of ₹50 lakh to its 70% subsidiary (outstanding at year end), and borrows ₹10 crore from a public sector bank. Its chairman is also on the board of an unrelated supplier.

mcqs.q: The purchase from the CFO's wife's firm is:
options: A related party transaction, as the CFO is KMP and his wife a relative
Not related, as the firm is separate
mcqs.explain: Key management personnel and their relatives are related parties, and so are enterprises over which they have significant influence. The wife's firm qualifies. In practice: disclose the ₹2 crore with balances.
mcqs.topic: Control, significant influence and who is a related party

mcqs.q: The bank loan of ₹10 crore is:
options: A related party transaction because the bank is state-owned
mcqs.explain: Providers of finance in the ordinary course are not related parties merely because of their dealings with the enterprise, whatever the amount. In practice: disclose the loan under borrowings, not AS 18.
mcqs.topic: Parties that are not related merely because of dealings

mcqs.q: Amount outstanding to be disclosed for the subsidiary loan in the separate statements:
mcqs.explain: The full ₹50 lakh outstanding with the subsidiary must be disclosed in the company's separate statements; being interest-free makes disclosure more, not less, important. It is eliminated only on consolidation. In practice: also state terms.
